text:
harper (DevEx): Quick thread: ran into a couple of annoying redwoodctl issues while trying to onboard a sample app for local testing. Thought I'd share findings and get opinions on fixes.

harper (DevEx): Scenario: dev follows sample-app README -> `redwoodctl install-script` -> `redwoodctl profile add sample-local` -> `redwoodctl local-serve` -> then `redwoodctl login --profile sample-local`. Several failures observed.

mika (QA): what failures exactly?

harper (DevEx): 1) installer doesn't create profile defaults for local-serve (like `local_redirect_uri`), so device-code flow launches but the callback URL mismatch causes auth error. 2) login retry logic retries without validating the token file contents (0-byte or partial file causes JSON parse errors). 3) sample app instructions assume `redwoodctl` on PATH; curl installer puts binary under ~/.redwood/bin on some dev machines in our sample images, not ~/.local/bin.

toni (Support): tickets for those already? we got two last week about the same flow.

harper (DevEx): Not filed yet; wanted to triage here first. I have a minimal repro: follow sample-app README, run `local-serve`, kill the process right after browser callback returns, then re-run login -> CLI errors with `auth: unexpected token` and then loops retries for 5 attempts.

mika (QA): I can automate the repro in CI. Suggest adding a flaky test that simulates abrupt kill during device callback. Will be good to catch regressions.

ezra (Platform): Thanks. Thoughts on fixes: - atomic token writes (tmpfile + rename) - validate token file before parsing (zero-byte => delete and warn) - local-serve should set default redirect URI and print explicit instructions for sample apps.

harper (DevEx): Also UX: sample README doesn't include a headless flow. Our CI and some devs can't open a browser. A `--print-url` flag for `redwoodctl login` or `--no-browser` with printed device code would help.

toni (Support): If we add `--print-url`, can we also surface a one-liner `curl` that completes the device flow for headless infra? Might be useful for quick debugging.

ezra (Platform): We should avoid documenting ways to bypass OAuth UX too easily. But printing the URL and device code is fine; the curl trick would be brittle. Instead, provide a short `headless.md` in sample-apps that explains `--print-url` and how to paste it into an external browser.

mika (QA): On the profile/defaults front, the sample-app template should include a `redwood.yml` snippet or a setup script that runs `redwoodctl profile set-defaults sample-local --redirect http://localhost:8080/callback`. Otherwise the UI mismatch is confusing.

harper (DevEx): Another weirdness: `redwoodctl profile list` prints nice table but doesn't show the source of the profile (config vs env vs migrated). For sample-apps it's helpful to know whether profile was auto-created by installer or user-added. Can we add a small column `source`?

ezra (Platform): Good idea. We'll add `source` with values `file|env|installer|migrated`. Low-risk change.

deploy-bot: deploy: sample-app image build succeeded (build-1245)

toni (Support): Two quick asks for the patch: 1) don't change cache layout without migration (we have enterprise users) 2) give clear KB steps for immediate workarounds (delete zero-byte token, rerun login, add ~/.redwood/bin to PATH).

ezra (Platform): Agreed. Patch plan: 
- atomic token write + fsync; on read, treat non-JSON/zero-length as invalid and remove before retry.
- add `--print-url` flag to login and `--no-browser` alias.
- update sample-app README with explicit profile defaults and headless steps.
- `redwoodctl profile list` add `source` column.
- add a CI flaky test for abrupt-kill during callback.

harper (DevEx): I'll file ISSUE-3001 and include the repro steps + small sample logs. Assigning to @ezra for the patch.

mika (QA): will queue the e2e and flaky tests once PR lands.

toni (Support): will draft KB article with immediate workarounds. Thanks!

harper (DevEx): Workaround in the meantime: ensure the installer path from README matches your environment (`echo $PATH`), delete `~/.redwood/cache/<profile>.token` if it's 0 bytes, then re-run `redwoodctl login --print-url` and complete auth in a browser.
